sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.
2. Appeal is admitted for hearing.
3. With the consent of learned counsel appearing for the parties, appeal is heard finally.

4 . This criminal appeal has been preferred by the appellant/complainant, being aggrieved by the judgment dated 09.12.2022 passed by the learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, District Jabalpur in Sessions Trial No. 600138/2013, whereby respondent Nos. 2 and 3/accused persons were acquitted of the charges under Sections 302/34 and in the alternative, Sections 304B and 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

5 . The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 16.03.2012, on receiving NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 2 CRA-1532-2023 information regarding the suspicious death of Smt.
Pushpa Bai, Deputy Superintendent of Police Mithlesh Tiwari reached the spot and registered Marg Prahlad Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161130524/
1 No. 24/2012.

sentences.text: Statements of the deceased's father Prahlad Patel, mother Chhoti Bai, brother Mukesh Kumar, sister-in-law Smt. Sita Bai, and Bhagwan Das were recorded.
It was stated that the deceased was married to Pradeep Patel of Hinauta, Bargi, on 25.02.2009, and was about 24 years of age at the time of her death.

It was alleged that since marriage, she was subjected to physical and mental cruelty by her husband Pradeep Patel, father-in-law Munna Patel, and mother-in-law Smt. Sushila Bai in connection with dowry demands, including two acres of land, a washing machine, a gas stove,
a sewing machine, and other articles.
It was further alleged that the deceased died after consuming a poisonous substance mixed in her tea.

On the basis of the statements of the parents, brother, and independent witnesses, Crime No. 147/2012 was registered against the accused for offences punishable under Section 304-B read with Section 34 IPC.
6.
Learned counsel for the appellant/complainant submitted that the impugned judgment dated 09.12.2022 is contrary to law and facts on record.
It was contended that the Trial Court failed to properly appreciate the evidence and erroneously acquitted respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

It was argued that the deceased died under unnatural and suspicious circumstances within seven years of her marriage and that the testimony of prosecution witnesses, particularly the parents and close relatives of the deceased, clearly establishes that she was subjected to continuous physical and mental cruelty in connection with dowry demands.

It was further submitted that medical and forensic evidence, including seizure of viscera, supports the prosecution case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 3 CRA-1532-2023 that the deceased consumed a poisonous substance.
According to the appellant, the Trial Court ignored material evidence and adopted a hyper- technical approach.
Therefore, it was prayed that the judgment of acquittal be set aside.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
8.
Prahlad Patel (PW-1), father of the deceased, stated in his examination-in-chief that the marriage of Pushpa Bai and Pradeep Patel was solemnized on 25.02.2009.

He stated that at the time of marriage, the accused demanded 60,000 in cash, a motorcycle, bed, cupboard, cooler, fridge,
dressing table, fan, and other household articles.

He further stated that after the first farewell,
Pushpa stayed at her matrimonial home for 5-6 days and thereafter returned to her parental home.

Subsequently, she again went to her matrimonial home but returned after three months,
complaining that her mother-in-law and sister-in-law had taken her jewellery and were demanding a washing machine, sewing machine, and two acres of land.
He stated that Pushpa stayed at her parental home for about one year and was reluctant to return to her matrimonial home due to harassment.
On 15.03.2012, Pushpa informed him over the phone that she had been sent to Hinauta.
On 16.03.2012 at about 9:30 a.m., she called and stated that her mother-in-law had forced her to drink tea, after which she experienced severe burning and abdominal pain.

She was taken first to Dr. Parihar at Bargi, then to Ramesh Baba, and finally admitted to Apex Hospital, Jabalpur,
where she died at about 6:30 p.m.
Panchnama proceedings were conducted thereafter (Ex. P-1 and Ex. P-2).

9. Smt. Chhoti Bai (PW-2), mother of the deceased, and Mukesh Patel NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 4 CRA-1532-2023 (PW-4), brother of the deceased, substantially corroborated the testimony of PW-1 in their examination-in-chief.

sentences.text: 10. Smt. Sita Bai (PW-3), sister-in-law of the deceased, did not support the prosecution case and was declared hostile.
However, in her cross- examination, she admitted that Pushpa had stayed at her parental home for a considerable period due to harassment.

11. Bhagwan Das (PW-5), an independent witness from the maternal village of the deceased, stated that Pushpa was subjected to dowry demands and harassment, due to which she resided at her parental home.

He further stated that after she was persuaded to return to her matrimonial home,
information was received within 4-5 days that she had died.

He stated that prior to her death,
Pushpa had complained of severe stomach pain after consuming tea given by her mother-in-law.
12. Dilip Kumar Patel (PW-6), cousin of the deceased, stated that Pushpa informed him that she was poisoned by her in-laws through tea and complained of severe burning and stomach pain.
He stated that she was taken to Apex Hospital, Jabalpur, where she died.
13. In cross-examination, Prahlad Patel (PW-1) admitted that no complaint was lodged with the police or any Panchayat regarding dowry harassment during the lifetime of the deceased.
He also admitted that at certain times Pushpa stayed happily at her matrimonial home and that no immediate complaint was made even after receiving her phone call on 15.03.2012.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 5 CRA-1532-2023 14.

Chhoti Bai (PW-2) admitted in cross-examination that there was no demand of dowry at the time of marriage and that on several occasions Pushpa and her relatives returned from the matrimonial home stating that everything was normal.
She further admitted that no complaint was ever lodged prior to Pushpa's death.

15. Mukesh Patel (PW-4) admitted that no complaint regarding dowry demand or harassment was made to the police during the lifetime of the deceased and that he disclosed such allegations for the first time before the Court.
16. Dr. Satish Bhaya (PW-7), who conducted the post-mortem, opined that the cause of death was undetermined and that viscera was preserved for chemical analysis.
He admitted that without chemical examination, he could not opine that the death was due to poisoning.

17. Investigating Officer Mithilesh Tiwari (PW-11) admitted in cross- examination that no dying declaration was recorded, statements of treating doctors were not recorded, no bed-head ticket or treatment papers were seized, no poisonous substance or tea cup was seized from the house, and that no prior complaint regarding dowry harassment existed.
18. Santosh Patel (DW-1) stated that no dowry demand was made at the time of marriage and that Pushpa was suffering from stomach ailments, for which she was regularly treated by Dr. Parihar.

19. Considering the aforesaid evidence and on perusal of record, it is found that the family members of the deceased have stated that the deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 6 Prahlad Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161130524/
3 CRA-1532-2023 had informed them over the mobile phone that her mother-in-law had mixed poison in her tea and compelled her to drink it, due to which her condition deteriorated.

sentences.text:
However,
the Investigating Officer has not conducted any investigation to verify whether the deceased had actually made any such call to her parents or brother from her mobile phone on the said date.

In fact, the Investigating Officer ought to have investigated this aspect by ascertaining whether the deceased had made any call to any of her relatives on the relevant date and by obtaining the call detail records in this regard.
However, no such call detail records have been obtained by the Investigating Officer.

Similarly, the Investigating Officer has not recorded the statement of the treating doctor to ascertain whether any relevant information was disclosed when the deceased was brought for medical treatment.
20. Upon re-appreciation of the entire evidence on record, this Court finds no perversity or illegality in the judgment of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court.

Although the death of the deceased occurred within seven years of marriage and was unnatural, the prosecution has failed to establish that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment in connection with dowry demands soon before her death as required under Section 304-B of the IPC.
The testimony of prosecution witnesses suffers from material contradictions and admissions and no prior complaint regarding dowry harassment was ever lodged during the lifetime of the deceased.
2 1 . Further, the prosecution has failed to prove the allegation of poisoning.
The medical evidence does not disclose a definite cause of death, no conclusive forensic report has been produced and no dying declaration was recorded.
The investigation also suffers from serious lapses including delay in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18133 7 CRA-1532-2023 registration of FIR and non-examination of material medical witnesses.

22. In view of the settled principle that an appellate court should not interfere with an order of acquittal unless the findings are perverse or wholly unreasonable and since the view taken by the Trial Court is a plausible one based on the evidence, therefore, this Court finds no ground for interference.
23. Accordingly, the criminal appeal is dismissed and the judgment of acquittal is affirmed.
24. Record of the trial Court be sent back.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (RATNESH CHANDRA SI  JUDGE JUDGE  sp/-
